title: Pressure vs. sacks: how three missing linemen became six sacks (Saints at Bears)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, no snaps logged) and no review files. The original football-film-room repo could not be read from this run (GitHub access for it isn't enabled). So there are no new misses to target. This lesson builds on Lesson 24 (count blockers vs. rushers) and Lesson 32 (backup linemen), using Sunday's Saints-Bears game.

The big idea: a "pressure" is any time a pass rusher gets to the QB fast enough to bother him.There are three kinds: a hurry (he has to throw early or move), a hit (he gets knocked down after throwing), and a sack (tackled before he throws).Sacks get the headlines. Pressures tell you why they happen.

Saints blockers are on the bottom row. Yellow = the spots where a starter was missing. Red = Bears rushers.

  1. A · The center. Starter Erik McCoy was out. The center calls out the protection for the whole line, so a backup there can mean missed assignments.
  2. B · Right tackle. Taliese Fuaga was out too. Undrafted rookie Mason Murphy started. Backup tackle Asim Richards was also out, so there was no one left to swap in.
  3. C · The rushers pick their target. Defensive coordinators line up their best rushers across from the weakest blockers.They also run stunts: two rushers cross paths to confuse a new lineman about who to block.
  4. D · The result. Tyler Shough was pressured on 23 of his 51 dropbacks: 45%. He was sacked 6 times, a season high. The Bears also scored a safety on him.For context, NFL offenses usually face pressure on about a third of dropbacks.

Why 51 dropbacks matters: the Saints trailed most of the game, so they had to throw (Lesson 51).More dropbacks plus a weak line equals more chances for sacks. That's how one injury report turns into six sacks.

Pressure cuts both ways: the Saints blitzed Caleb Williams too. Against extra rushers he went 5 of 12 for 39 yards, with a TD and an INT.A blitz is a gamble (Lesson 6). It worked for New Orleans on those snaps, but Chicago won 21-13 because its own rush never stopped.

Why it matters for bets: sacks cost yards and end drives. That pushes totals down and QB passing yards down.Tonight, two lines are missing a starter: Bengals RG Dalton Risner (out) and Commanders LT Laremy Tunsil (IR).The brief's Burrow 300+ lean counts on Cincinnati's line holding up without Risner. If Burrow is sacked early and often, that lean is in trouble.

For your Film Room drill: before the game, read the inactives and note any backup linemen.During the game, watch the QB's feet after the snap. If he's moving or throwing early on most drop-backs, pressure is high, even without sacks.Log the snap run or pass as usual. Add a note when the QB is hurried: those snaps often turn into checkdowns or throwaways.

Connecting the dots: Lesson 24 taught counting blockers against rushers. Lesson 32 showed why backup guards matter. This lesson adds the scoreboard: a weak spot plus a team that has to pass is how pressure piles up into sacks.

Video: search YouTube for "Saints Bears 2026 highlights Shough sacked" and "what is a QB pressure PFF explained."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 7: Read the snap)

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a kind of QB pressure?
quiz.w: Hurries, hits and sacks are all pressures. A false start is a penalty on the offense before the snap.

quiz.q: Tyler Shough was pressured on 23 of 51 dropbacks. About what share is that?
quiz.w: 23 ÷ 51 ≈ 45%. NFL offenses usually face pressure on about a third of dropbacks.

quiz.q: Why did the Saints' missing center matter even on plays where no one rushed through his spot?
o: The center snaps the ball for punts only
The center calls the protection for the whole line
quiz.w: The center usually sets the blocking calls. A backup there can lead to missed assignments anywhere on the line.

quiz.q: Before tonight's game, which injury connects most directly to the brief's Burrow 300+ lean?
o: Terry McLaurin out for the season
quiz.w: Burrow throws behind Cincinnati's line. A backup guard means more risk of pressure, which can cut his yards.
